sections.skill: Estimate student loan payments and judge borrowing against expected earnings

questions.prompt: Kira borrows $27,000 at 6% on a 10-year plan. Her payment is $299.76 a month. How much interest will she pay in total?
questions.intro: Most federal loans offer a standard 10-year plan. Total paid = payment × 120; interest = total paid − amount borrowed.

questions.prompt: A guideline says total student debt should not exceed the expected first-year salary. Kira expects $45,000. Which borrowing fits?
questions.intro: Return on investment (ROI) compares what education costs with what it is likely to earn. A common rule of thumb: keep total borrowing at or below your expected starting salary.

questions.prompt: Kira lost her job and cannot make her federal loan payment. What should she do first?

choices.text: Stop paying and ignore the letters
Take a payday loan to pay it
Use a credit card to make the payments

questions.intro: Federal loans offer options such as deferment, forbearance, and income-driven repayment. Repayment rules changed in 2025-2026, so check StudentAid.gov for current plans. Default can lead to collections and wage garnishment.
questions.feedback: Contacting the loan servicer early opens options and avoids default.
